summary: Anthony C. Yu was a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago, where he served as a professor from circa 1968 to 2005.

Anthony Cerulli works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago from 2001 to 2007 and was appointed Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin–Madison circa 2014.

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak in 1928, later serving there as a lecturer in Chinese (1946) and professor (1956–1975).

Anthony Kennedy Warder was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his doctorate at SOAS University of London under John Brough, taught at the University of Edinburgh (1955–1963), and was a professor at the University of Toronto (1963–1990).

Anthony Tribe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol and Oxford under Paul Williams, Steven Collins, and Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at the University of Montana (1997) and University of Arizona (2020).

Anthony W. Barber specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1984 and held a post at the University of Calgary, attested in 1998.

Antoine Meillet worked in linguistics, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied under Darmesteter, Lévi, and Saussure in Paris, later holding professorships at the EPHE, INALCO (1902–1906), and the Collège de France (1905–1936).

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a linguist, historian, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He taught at INALCO, the Collège de France (1806–1838), and the University of Paris (1815), also serving as president of the Société Asiatique.

Antoine-Léonard de Chézy was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Louis-Mathieu Langlès. He worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, INALCO, and held the Sanskrit chair at the Collège de France (1815–1832).

Anton Boller was an Austrian scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a lecturer and extraordinary professor at the University of Vienna, becoming a full professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit there in 1855.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin circa 1828–1831, later teaching there from 1849 to 1852, and held a post at the Royal Danish Library.

Anton Schiefner worked in Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Humboldt University of Berlin, later working at the Imperial Academy of Sciences and Saint Petersburg Roman Catholic Theological Academy (1860–1873).
Anton Westermann was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He completed his habilitation at Leipzig University in 1830 and served there as co-director from 1830 to 1865.

Antonino Forte was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (circa 1976–2006), the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, Hōbōgirin, and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.
Antonio T. de Nicolás was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD from Fordham University and served on the faculty at Stony Brook University from circa 1969 to 2000.

Antonio Terrone specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and has served as a scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
Anuj Misra is a scholar who studied under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker from circa 2013 to 2016.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Calcutta under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, later teaching Pali there (attested 1943) and directing the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1981).

Arata Okayama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, and Peking University under Xianlin Ji, later serving as professor at the University of Tokyo from 1995 to 2012.

Archibald Edward Gough was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He held professorships at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Presidency University, and served as principal of Aliah University between 1878 and 1895.
